blocks.content: No person shall be a citizen of India by virtue of article 5, or be deemed to be a citizen of India by virtue of article 6 or article 8, if he has voluntarily acquired the citizenship of any foreign State.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 9 stipulates that any person who voluntarily acquires the citizenship of a foreign State ceases to be a citizen of India.
The Citizenship Act, 1955 details three distinct procedures for the loss of Indian citizenship: Renunciation, Termination, and Deprivation.
Renunciation is a voluntary declaration made by a citizen of full age and capacity to give up Indian nationality.
Termination operates automatically by law when an Indian citizen voluntarily acquires foreign citizenship.
Deprivation is a compulsory termination imposed by the Central Government on grounds such as fraud, disloyalty to the Constitution, or illegal trade during war.

rows: Citizen must be of full age and capacity; registration can be withheld during war.
Triggers immediately upon voluntary acquisition of foreign nationality.
Applied in cases of registration obtained by fraud, disloyalty to Constitution, or unlawful trade/communication during war.

items: Article 9 only covers cases where foreign citizenship was voluntarily acquired before the commencement of the Constitution; post-commencement cases are governed by the Citizenship Act, 1955.
When a person renounces Indian citizenship, every minor child of that person also loses Indian citizenship, but such a child may resume Indian citizenship within one year after attaining full age.
Deprivation of citizenship applies strictly to citizens who acquired citizenship by registration or naturalisation.
